subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar accept shared persistent configuration as an authority for launching user-configured local commands when quota or provider events occur?
rationale: The implementation can be mechanically corrected, but whether a monitoring app should introduce persistent arbitrary process execution—and what trust guidance must accompany it—is a repository product and security-boundary choice rather than a code-review inference.

options.title: Approve after lossless editor repair
options.body: Accept the opt-in direct-exec design after argv round-tripping is fixed and the config trust boundary is clearly documented.

options.title: Narrow to CLI-only configuration
options.body: Keep hook execution but omit the settings editor until a safe structured argument-editing and trust UX is designed.

options.title: Decline local execution hooks
options.body: Close the feature direction if persistent config-driven process execution is outside CodexBar's intended observability scope.

recommendation.title: Approve after lossless editor repair
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in direct-exec design after argv round-tripping is fixed and the config trust boundary is clearly documented.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, steipete is the best available authority for accepting or rejecting the new command-execution product boundary.
